messages:
alex: Heads-up — morning batch saw 3 nodes with repeated Xid 79 / ECC spikes during the nightly stress run. I pulled logs but it's slow to triage. Thinking we should ship a tiny 'gpu-log-preview' agent on prod nodes that collects a short, scrubbed bundle and posts a summary to the incident channel.

maria: Can you paste the minimal set of things we need? ops is wary of shipping anything that touches kernel logs without filtering.

alex: Minimal: `dmesg --ctime -T --level=err,warn`, `journalctl -k -n 200 --no-pager`, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,uuid,ecc.errors.uncorrected.total --format=csv,noheader,nounits`, and the last `~200` lines of the workload container logs. Agent should: 1) redact PII/paths, 2) compress to <= 128KB, 3) compute a short fingerprint of card errors for quick grouping.

sam: Love the fingerprint idea. Suggest we compute a deterministic key like: `sha1(uuid + pci_id + ecc_counts + nearest-dmesg-hash)` so signals from different nodes for the same card map together.

jin: Hardware note — pci_id can change if BIOS reassigns resources after hotplug. Use PCI slot (e.g., `lspci -nn | grep -i nvidia`) + vendor/device + serial where available. UUID is best if present.

maria: Security: agent must run as non-root where possible. `dmesg` needs CAP_SYSLOG. Could run as a privileged short-lived pod executed by node-agent instead. Also we need opt-in per cluster/region (APAC has extra rules).

alex: Agreed. Implementation sketch: run as k8s daemonset with hostPID namespace, single-run mode triggered by `gpu-watchdog` when Xid/ECC thresholds hit, not continuous. That reduces attack surface.

sam: For parsing heuristics: we should capture common Xid strings and map variants to canonical codes. Example pattern list: `Xid 79`, `Xid 31`, `GPU fault: ECC error`, `nvmlDeviceGetXidErrors`. Try to attach the immediate `dmesg` window +/- 60s.

alex: Example output we want posted to slack (compact):
```
diag-bot: GPU-Preview: node=gpu-234; cards=4; fingerprints=[f1:sha1, f2:sha1]; top_msgs=["Xid 79 at 2024-03-12 03:12:45","ECC uncorrected on GPU1"]; recommended_action=Drain+replace suspect GPU1; bundle=/s3/diag/2024/1715004321-gpu-234.tgz
```

maria: Storage: upload bundles to S3 with short TTL (30 days) and KMS-encrypt. Keep the slack post only the summary + a signed download URL. No raw logs inline.

jin: Also add `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTILIZATION,MEMORY` snapshot. Some ECC systems report counters in ranges and it's useful to capture both corrected/uncorrected counts.

sam: For quick triage, a tiny parsing snippet we can reuse: `grep -E "Xid|ECC|GPU fault|nvml" | tail -n 50` plus a dmesg time-slice. But we should normalize timestamps to ISO and include node-local clock offset info.

alex: Ops question: how aggressive are we on auto-drain? I'd prefer only recommend; automated drains need an explicit opt-in policy per fleet. We can surface risk score 0..10 where >7 suggests manual intervene or auto if teams opted in.

maria: +1. We'll create a new `fleet-policies` flag for `auto_drain_on_hardware_failure` per pool. Default: false.

sam: Metrics/events: emit a `gpu_diag.preview_created` metric with tags {node, region, card_count, fingerprint_count, reason}. Also increment counters when agent fails to collect (permission denied, size limit).

jin: Edge case: card flakiness that shows only ECC corrected events — that's noisy. We should compute a short-term rate (events/min) and compare to baseline per card model. If model baseline high (older cards), lower risk score.

alex: Nice. Implementation to-dos: 1) prototype agent (Go) with minimal deps, 2) parser lib (python) for triage pipelines, 3) diag-bot slack poster + signed S3 upload, 4) policy flags in infra-config. I can prototype the Go collector this week.

maria: I'll draft RBAC + KMS/S3 policy language and the opt-in fleet flag. Also will list regions where extra approval required (APAC-reg, eu-regulated).

sam: I'll work the parser and the fingerprint algorithm. Can we reuse existing Xid normalization rules from `gpu-telemetry` repo? If that repo has a permissive license we can vendor a subset.

jin: I'll validate hardware identifiers on a matrix of our host types. Some older HBAs expose limited serial info; we'll fallback gracefully.

diag-bot: scheduled run triggered by event: `XID_ALERT` -> run collector -> upload -> post-summary.

alex: Quick config snippet for the daemonset trigger (proposal):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gpu-log-preview-config
data:
  trigger_threshold: "3" # Xid events in 5m
  window_seconds: "300"
  max_bundle_kb: "128"
  auto_drain_threshold: "8"
```

maria: Can we add a `redact_patterns` list in the config for cluster owners to customize file/path redaction?

alex: Yes. Add `redact_patterns: /home/.*, /var/lib/containers/.*` by default.

sam: Next steps: I'll open a RFC with the parser spec and sample normalized output. Alex, can you drop the proto collector binary in a draft PR so we can iterate?

alex: Will do. Target: prototype PR by EOD Friday. If anyone sees blocking compliance items call them out now.

maria: Noted. Please include an audit log entry when agent runs and who requested it. For forensics we need traceability.

jin: One more: include `nvidia-persistence-mode` state snapshot. Sometimes persistence mode changes hide errors between reboots.

sam: Good catch.

alex: Thanks all — I'll spin up the prototype and tag you.

maria: :thumbsup:
